llm.summary: This VMware policy helper is mostly coherent, but it needs Review because a shared safety layer documents a simple global policy-disable switch and other under-scoped security behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill uses local VMware policy and audit files as expected, but it also documents checking OPENAI_API_KEY merely to infer the agent type, and the global VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED environment variable can bypass policy checks without approval or scoping in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a disclosed uv package install for vmware-policy with Bash allowed and no executable files in the submitted artifact. The package is also described as an automatic dependency of the VMware skill family, so users should treat it as shared infrastructure rather than a standalone helper.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is marked user-invocable false and exposes no MCP tools itself; its instructions are primarily integration guidance for other VMware skills. The scope is broad across 156+ tools, and some security guarantees, especially universal sanitization, are described more strongly than the artifact can prove.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local audit logging to ~/.vmware/audit.db is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with rotation and no network export claimed. However, logs can include operational metadata, parameters, results, agent identity, workflow ID, and user, and the export guidance does not clearly warn that those logs may be sensitive.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is audit logging, policy enforcement, sanitization, and read-only gating across VMware skills, which is coherent, but the artifacts also document VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a global bypass and note that missing PyYAML silently allows all operations, both of which materially weaken the enforcement purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing in environments where VMware tools can make real infrastructure changes. The main issue is not hidden malware; it is that a shared policy layer documents easy fail-open or bypass paths. Operators should restrict who can set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED, verify PyYAML and policy rules are installed, protect ~/.vmware/audit.db and exports as sensitive records, and avoid relying on the claimed sanitization/read-only guarantees without checking the actual installed package behavior.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: Agent detection for audit attribution is purpose-aligned, but using OPENAI_API_KEY as a presence marker is overbroad for that purpose even though the artifact says key values are not logged.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact discloses the environment-variable check and says no API keys or tokens are logged; that reduces the concern, but the credential-bearing variable is still touched for a non-credential purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The CLI reference confirms VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypasses policy checks while operations continue as bypassed, which is under-scoped for a shared policy-enforcement layer.
[SDI-4] expected: Sanitization is central to the skill, but the setup guide's statement that all API response text passes through sanitize() is broader than the manual integration examples can substantiate.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The capabilities reference confirms a full policy bypass via VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1, with audit logging but no artifact-backed approval, time limit, or production restriction.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit export is a core workflow, but the documented examples encourage full JSON export without a clear confidentiality warning for operational audit metadata.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The status and environment-variable sections confirm the bypass is a normal documented state, not just an isolated debugging note, which is a material concern for shared guardrail infrastructure.
